text:
meera: heads-up - saw a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate on a private customer cluster after yesterday's kernel-selection landing. 80% -> 18% on a steady workload :grimacing:

kyle: ugh. which kernel change? the sequence-length optimization or the new int8 path?

meera: landed both, but toggling seq-opt off restores hits. suspect keying + sequence bucketing interaction. reproducer attached below.

sam: can you paste the hit-rate timeline? rough numbers are fine.

meera: sure, here's a short sample from perf dashboard for that tenant (private, VPC):

```
window_start,cache_hits,requests,hit_rate
2026-08-01T10:00Z,4000,5000,80.0
2026-08-01T12:00Z,900,5000,18.0
2026-08-01T12:05Z,950,5200,18.2
2026-08-01T12:10Z,1200,5400,22.2
```

meera: timeline aligns with when the runtime switched kernel selection to prefer packed-int8 for >512 context.

lee: interesting. any difference between hosted and private? we haven't seen this on hosted infra, right?

meera: correct, hosted stays ~78-82% for same request shapes. only private and one dedicated pool show the regression.

kyle: could be cache signature generation adding a salt derived from device/driver info that changes between kernels. if the signature includes kernel_identifier + session_id, that would fragment keys.

sam: i pulled a few raw cache keys from both environments. samples (hex truncated):
```
hosted: ab12ef...:sig_v1:ctx512:pref_L
private: ab12ef...:sig_v2:ctx512:pref_L
```

sam: note the sig_v1 vs sig_v2. looks like a schema bump when selecting int8 path.

meera: exactly. sig_v2 was introduced to track kernel feature flags so we could invalidate when switching kernels. bug is sig_v2 currently includes a nondeterministic entropy byte (container start hash) in private deployments because the agent sets runtime_id differently in VPC mode.

lee: wow. so hosted sets runtime_id = global_runtime_hash, private uses container_id which rotates on restart -> accidental per-container key variance.

kyle: that fits why hosted unaffected. hosted control plane pins runtime_id. private agent had a fallback to local container metadata when control-plane metadata timed out.

sam: quick patch idea: remove runtime_id from cache signature and instead include a stable kernel fingerprint (model-arch + kernel-version string). keep runtime_id only in telemetry.

meera: agreed. but we need a short-term mitigation: we can roll back the seq-opt kernel selection on private pools while we ship a deterministic-signature patch.

ops-bot: deploy requested by @meera - rollback seq-opt on dedicated/private pools. CI job queued (job id: 85212). :white_check_mark:

lee: also want to audit cache keying logic: search for any use of ephemeral metadata (container_id, hostname, pod_uniq) in signature builder. I can run a grep tomorrow.

kyle: profiling notes: when hit-rate drops, latency climbs ~12-15% even though kernel throughput improved. so net perf worse for that workload. we should add a perf regression test that measures end-to-end tail latency and hit-rate under sequence prefixes.

sam: adding to backlog: RG-PR-211 add e2e perf test for prefix-caching hit-rate across kernel toggles.

meera: immediate plan: 1) ops roll back seq-opt on affected pools (in flight), 2) kyle to change signature builder to remove ephemeral entropy (PR incoming), 3) lee to run grep + infra audit, 4) sam to author e2e test. aiming for patch + release by EOD tomorrow.

kyle: i'll open the PR now and tag @meera for review. small change, unit tests included.

meera: thanks. once PR is merged we can re-enable seq-opt behind an explicit stable-fingerprint flag for private.

lee: noted - i'll grep for other usages and add a short doc about 'signature hygiene' for agents operating in VPC/on-prem vs hosted.

sam: FYI: captured customer's cache logs and shared with support (redact done). they saw client-level retries due to increased latency, so this is higher priority.

meera: thanks all. will follow up in the morning with rollback status. :thumbsup:
